record.title: Combined Compose service identity can carry platform authority into the demo image
record.description: Source review confirms the documented combined launch (docs/DEMO.md:20) lists deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml before deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml, and both files declare services.api under the same project name graveshift. Under standard Compose multi-file merge semantics (confirmed here by a parent-side config render of scratch copies), the later demo definition sets image, build.context and x-app environment/networks but does not use !reset or !override (no such directives exist in deploy/compose/), so the platform api definition's environment keys (internal tokens, OAuth JWT secret, root-bootstrap fields at graveshift.compose.yml:94-100), build.dockerfile, command, profiles and core network are not cleared by source. A concrete lower-trust principal exists: .kiro/agents/chaos-witch.json:9 denies shell and denies fs_write except under examples/**, so it can alter the example build context, Dockerfile and launcher but not deploy/platform source. The finding does NOT assert that the unchanged combination leaks real secrets: the retained platform command src/main.ts and build.dockerfile deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile are absent from the example context (verified: no examples/haunted-candy-shop/src/main.ts and no examples/haunted-candy-shop/deploy/), and the retained api profile is not enabled by the documented command. A trusted parent-side `docker compose config --format json` render of scratch copies with a dummy marker confirmed that, with the api profile enabled, the merged api service selects the examples-controlled image while retaining the platform credential environment keys and the core network; no image build or process execution was performed, and delivery of real credentials remains owner/conditional.

trace.description: Line 9 denies shell and denies fs_write on ** with exclude examples/**; the agent prompt at line 12 restates 'Write only under examples/' and 'Never touch source packages.' This is a concrete lower-trust source-editing role for the example Dockerfile and launcher; the candidate also covers any equivalently scoped example contributor.

Line 5 copies src into the image; line 8 sets CMD bun src/api-main.ts. An examples-only writer controls the code packaged into this lower-trust image and can add examples-local files (e.g. src/main.ts and a compatible deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile under the example context) matching fields retained by the merged service, with no platform-source edit.

services.api (line 78) is opt-in via profiles: [api] (line 82), builds from deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile (line 85), runs bun src/main.ts (line 88), holds internal-token/JWT/root-bootstrap environment fields (lines 94-100, all ${VAR:-} defaults) and joins core (line 105). Empty defaults and the profile gate are material prerequisites, not an observed grant.

Line 20 documents 'docker compose -f deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml -f deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml up -d --build', selecting support first and demo second so same-named service definitions merge; line 81 repeats the order for down. The command does not pass --profile api, so the inherited API profile must be enabled separately for the colliding service to run.

trace.scope: Merged api workload identity and environment
trace.description: services.api (line 23) merges <<: *app (line 24): example build context and haunted-candy-shop:local image (lines 7-9), candy network (line 15), demo environment map (lines 16-20). No reset directives clear the platform fields from the earlier file. The claimed minimum boundary result is a runnable lower-trust image receiving a dummy platform-secret marker; retained core membership is a second configuration effect, without assuming any successful management operation.

evidence.description: fs_write deny on ** with exclude examples/** and shell deny on line 8 supply the limited example-editing role rather than assuming deploy-file write access; line 12 prompt reinforces the scope.
The platform API retains profiles: [api]; a combined run without this profile does not establish execution of the colliding API service, and the documented command at DEMO.md:20 omits it.

build.dockerfile is deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile, which a context-only override retains under the example build context. Verified absent from the current example tree, so the unchanged combination is not established buildable.
command invokes bun src/main.ts. The example provides api-main.ts and worker-main.ts but no src/main.ts, so an unchanged runnable leak is not established.

API environment contains GRAVESHIFT_API_INTERNAL_TOKEN, plus GRAVESHIFT_DAEMON_INTERNAL_TOKEN (95), GRAVESHIFT_OAUTH_JWT_SECRET (96) and root-bootstrap fields (97-100), all sourced from the owner environment with empty defaults. No real values were read or copied.
The platform API joins core, the network shared by the read proxy, broker, database, actuator and Prometheus. The demo override does not explicitly reset this network list.
x-app sets build.context to ../../examples/haunted-candy-shop (line 8), image haunted-candy-shop:local (line 9), networks [candy] (line 15) and a demo environment map (lines 16-20).

The demo uses the identical api service key with <<: *app and no environment/network/profile/command reset or !reset/!override tag (verified none in deploy/compose), supplying the source-visible conflicting handoff.

The normal example launcher consumes process.env via createApi({ env: process.env }); an examples-controlled compatible launcher likewise reads the environment delivered to its container. Actual delivery of a dummy privileged marker remains untested.

The combined support-first, demo-second invocation is maintained documentation (also line 81). Its default profile omission and inherited build/command failures must be accounted for when evaluating applicability.

record.root_cause: deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml and deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml assign different trust roles to the same Compose service key api. The later demo definition overrides image and build.context but, in source, contains no environment/network/profile/command/build.dockerfile reset directives, so under standard Compose merge the platform API's credential environment, core network, api profile, src/main.ts command and deploy/compose/bun.Dockerfile path can be retained. An actor with write authority confined to examples/** can then control the selected image's build and runtime inputs without editing platform configuration. The source-visible prerequisites (api profile co-enablement, nonempty owner credentials, and a runnable examples-supplied variant supplying the absent Dockerfile/entrypoint) are not established as met.
record.intended_behavior: A lower-trust example image must not inherit platform credentials or networking.

conditions.description: The observation was a trusted parent-side `docker compose config --format json` render of bounded dummy-data scratch copies of the two maintained manifests; no container was run, and deployment preconditions are recorded in the source trace.

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of the lower-trust capability described in the title.

instructions: Parent-side only: copy deploy/compose/graveshift.compose.yml and deploy/compose/demo.compose.yml to scratch; in the demo copy set `security_opt: !reset [no-new-privileges:true]` (the unchanged pair fails Compose v5 with duplicate no-new-privileges:true); run `docker compose --profile api -f <support copy> -f <demo copy> config --format json` with an 11-key dummy environment. The rendered api service is the single structured observed result; no container harness was used and no target source was edited.
execution.observed_result: When the api profile is enabled, the merged services.api selects the examples-controlled image while retaining the platform credential environment fields and the core network. The unchanged pair fails Compose v5 validation because of a duplicate security_opt item; resolving that in a scratch copy produced the rendered result.

remediation.strategy: Use distinct Compose service keys and explicit !reset directives for environment and networks, or separate Compose projects, and validate the combined render in CI.

impact.reason: Delivers platform credentials and core-network membership to the example workload.
